name: Remotion WebM Alpha Overlay Export
use_when: A transparent Remotion animation is intended for supported browser playback.
The delivery target accepts WebM alpha and smaller files matter.
The overlay is a web asset rather than an editor interchange file.
avoid_when: The transparent file will be handed to Premiere, Resolve, Final Cut, CapCut, or an unknown editor.
The browser or platform alpha support is uncertain.
The overlay has critical brand colors or soft edges that need editor-grade interchange.
An opaque final MP4 is the only delivery needed.

timeline_pattern.fallback_rule: Render an opaque fallback with identical duration, fps, and timing when browser support is not guaranteed.
timeline_pattern.support_rule: Document the intended browser/platform instead of treating WebM alpha as universal.

motion.rule: Match fps and duration to the web player or parent page timing so the transparent animation does not drift.

keyframe_values.codec: Use VP8 or VP9 depending on project support.

sound.rule: Keep sound outside the transparent WebM unless the web component explicitly requires synchronized audio.

captions.rule: Do not use stylized WebM alpha text as the only accessibility caption layer for important speech.

color.rule: Check compression and edge color over the actual page/background colors before approving.

implementation.ffmpeg: Encode PNG frames with libvpx-vp9 and pix_fmt yuva420p for a browser-targeted transparent WebM; test playback in the target browser.
implementation.remotion: Render with --image-format=png --codec=vp9 or vp8 and --pixel-format=yuva420p; create a separate opaque fallback when needed.
implementation.blender: Use WebM/VP9 alpha only for web delivery after browser tests; otherwise prefer RGBA frames or ProRes 4444.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Do not assume CapCut will import WebM alpha correctly; use ProRes/PNG sequence or pre-composite if needed.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Avoid WebM alpha as the primary Premiere handoff; prefer ProRes 4444.

common_mistakes: Using WebM alpha for editor interchange because it previews in a browser.
Skipping the opaque fallback for unsupported playback environments.
Forgetting PNG frame format before alpha encoding.
Testing over only one background color.
Treating browser support as stable without a target-platform check.
qc: Target browser plays the alpha file correctly.
Opaque fallback has identical timing and content.
Edges stay clean over actual page/background colors.
File is not used as the primary editor handoff unless support was proven.
No important caption/accessibility content exists only in the decorative alpha layer.
